supportMap.description: Hitchens contrasts a quantum account of matter's origin with the destructive and wasteful cosmic outcome offered as benign design.
supportMap.anchor: of what benign design could that conceivably be a part

supportMap.description: Current quantum knowledge is said to make an origin from nothing less contradictory than it initially appears.
supportMap.anchor: nothing from nothing isn't as much of a contradiction as it may seem

supportMap.description: The future threats named include Andromeda's collision with our galaxy and the possibility that our sun will blow up.
supportMap.anchor: whether our sun will join the billions of suns that have blown up

supportMap.description: Hubble's red shift and a newly discovered increasing expansion rate are offered as evidence that the universe is flying apart faster.
supportMap.anchor: we're flying apart faster than we thought

supportMap.description: The extinction of nearly every species created on Earth is characterized as waste, profusion, and cruelty rather than benevolence.
supportMap.anchor: 99.8% of every species created on Earth since it started has been dispensed with

supportMap.description: The proposed divine ruler is characterized as a capricious tyrant modeled on human authority, supporting the conclusion that humans made gods.

boundaryJustification.startWhy: Event 3120 is the first event that states the quantum-origin account; events 3115–3119 only introduce Krauss and name his lecture.
boundaryJustification.endWhy: Event 3200 completes the human-projection conclusion by identifying the creators as beings close to chimpanzees; event 3201 is only a trailing thanks.
boundaryJustification.removedPrefix: Events 3066–3119 were removed because they discuss Hawking, the death of philosophy, historical natural philosophy, and introduce a recommended lecture without stating the retained origin argument.
boundaryJustification.removedSuffix: Event 3201 was removed because its sole word, 'it shows thank,' is a closing courtesy after the completed conclusion and supplies no premise or qualification.

repairs.longerCompleteArgumentRationale: Events 3120–3127 are required for the quantum-origin alternative; events 3149–3157 separately supply future galactic collision and stellar destruction; events 3158–3168 supply accelerating expansion; events 3176–3181 supply mass extinction; and events 3182–3200 supply the capricious, human-modeled ruler conclusion. Removing either endpoint would drop the origin claim or the final human-projection basis, while the intervening components are all named in the immutable summaries.
